titleReview: Gripping and emotional - couldn’t put it down
reviewDescription: Web of Destiny pulls you in from the very first page and doesn’t let go.
Set against the gritty backdrop of early 1900s London, it follows young Marie Charlotte Jensen as she struggles to survive in a world stacked against her.
The writing is vivid and emotionally raw, with characters that feel incredibly real. Marie’s strength and vulnerability make her a protagonist you root for with your whole heart.
This is historical fiction at its most gripping—honest, atmospheric, and deeply moving.
I'm already reaching for the next book in the series.

titleReview: A Heartbreaking Tale of Resilience and Grit
reviewDescription: The author took me into a world of a young girl orphaned and in terrible situations, but she never seemed to lose hope. Her vivid imagination sustains her throughout her hardships and I found myself rooting for her.

Mysterious characters that I anxiously looked forward to explanations of who they were and how this unfortunate soul, Marie Charlotte, would be saved from the misery of the life she was thrown into. Her spunky character makes you root for her to be pulled out of the poverty she has been in since her birth mother died.

Although we, the readers, can't be sure that her birth mother is actually dead for at one point in the book, a mysterious woman arrives in town reminiscing about how the town has changed, she has changed along with her name. The author leaves the story hanging and the reader searching for answers in the next book.

I picked this up on a whim and ended up staying up way too late because I couldn't put it down. Marie Charlotte's story is both heartbreaking and inspiring at the same time. The setting in 1910s Norway really comes alive through Lunde's writing.

Her journey from the orphanage to living with Olga and then everything that follows just pulls you right in. I found myself rooting for this tough little girl who refuses to give up no matter how bad things get.

What I loved most was how real Marie felt as a character. She's not perfect, she tells stories and fibs sometimes, but she's got this incredible spirit that shines through even in the darkest moments. The way she stands up to bullies like Didrik and survives situations that would break most people is just amazing.

The historical details are fantastic too. You really get a sense of what life was like for poor kids during that time period. Its educational but never feels like a history lesson because the story is so engaging. I have to warn you though, this book deals with some heavy topics. There's poverty, abuse, and violence that might be tough for some readers. But its handled tastefully and serves the story well.

titleReview: A Story of Resilience and Hope
reviewDescription: I followed every step of Marie with my heart in my throat—from the cold and cruelty of the asylum to the small moments of kindness that gave her hope again.

The setting in early 20th-century Oslo is beautifully portrayed, and the writing captures both the harshness of her environment and the inner strength of a girl who refuses to give up. It’s a tough story, yes, but also a hopeful one: even in the midst of abandonment, it’s possible to resist and seek a different destiny.
I love historical dramas, especially when they're character-driven, and this book set in 1910s Oslo sounded really compelling.
Marie Charlotte Jensen's life is tough, growing up in the shadows and treated like a slave. But her imagination and the hints of a hidden past really draw you in.

I felt for her as she started questioning who her father was and who the mysterious Mamsell is. It's a quiet struggle, but you can feel her growing courage. It deals with emotionally intense themes realistically, which I appreciated. It's a powerful story of survival and finding your own path.
